name: Planning Together
title: Planning Together
answer: Planning together means teacher teams use shared time and AI drafts to improve lessons, assessments, and curriculum coverage. It matters because separate AI planning duplicates work, while team review saves time and helps teachers learn from one another. It also helps teams spot standards that may be missing or lightly covered.

sections.body: Professional learning communities give teachers time to share lessons, study student work, and solve problems. AI can make that time more productive by producing shared drafts, such as a common assessment, that the team then revises together. The problem is duplicated effort: when each teacher plans the same unit alone with AI, the team repeats hours of work. A team that divides the unit, drafts with AI, and reviews each other's work saves time and improves quality. The review step is where teachers learn from each other.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a grade level team, teachers can divide a unit, use AI to draft parts, and then review each other's work in a meeting. A team might use AI to draft a common assessment and spend its meeting revising it together. Teams can also run a standards audit, using AI to compare unit plans against state standards and flag standards that appear missing or lightly covered. The team checks each flag because tools can misread how a standard is addressed, and the audit guides revisions for the following year. The text gives no separate grade bands beyond grade level teams.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The supplied text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It describes a practical approach to teacher planning rather than citing research. So this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI can misread how a standard is addressed, so the team must check each flag from a standards audit. The tool can draft, but the team revises the common assessment and decides what to keep or change. The review step belongs to teachers because that is where they learn from each other. The text does not say AI should make final curriculum decisions. Those decisions stay with the team.
